title: Route & Model Tail-Latency Guardian: streaming vs blocking SLI dashboard
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Ship a dashboard and SLI comparator that makes it trivial for Platform/ProdEng to detect and triage tail latency regressions split by model and route, with an explicit streaming vs blocking (non-streaming) decomposition. This ticket covers the telemetry queries, trace/span hooks to expose io_mode, dashboard panels, alertable SLI definitions (p95/p99), and rollout plan.

Why this is needed:
- Current latency boards surface aggregate percentiles but obscure pathological tails when large streaming workloads mix with blocking requests on the same route/model.
- Customers (internal and external) have hit scenarios where p50 looks fine but p99 spikes correlate with streaming bursts or specific model versions.

Scope / Deliverables:
- Add/verify trace/span attributes: model_name, model_version, route, io_mode {streaming, blocking}, request_shape (tokens_in, tokens_out), kv_cache_hit. Instrumentation PR: link to github PR in attachments.
- Metrics/Logs pipeline: ensure the metrics pipeline (Prometheus/ClickHouse ingestion) emits histogram buckets and raw p50/p95/p99 counters by (route, model_name, model_version, io_mode). Work with infra on retention vs cost.
- Dashboard panels:
  1) Tail-Latency Skyline: per-route per-model p50/p95/p99 sparkline grid (90-day), with toggle for io_mode split.
  2) Streaming vs Blocking Contrast: stacked percentile delta heatmap showing p95_p99(streaming) - p95_p99(blocking) to highlight which routes suffer during streaming bursts.
  3) ServePath Waterfall Linker: for any selected point, link to traced span waterfall (trace id) and raw logs.
  4) Cohort Explorer: filter by request_shape, token buckets, and kv_cache_hit to isolate workload drivers.
  5) SLI Comparator: baseline vs candidate model_version comparisons across percentiles and io_modes.
- SLI definitions and alerting: template SLOs for p95 and p99 per route (with dynamic thresholds) and an automated alert playbook (runbook link included).
- Acceptance criteria: panels render within Console target latency; percentile calculations match offline ClickHouse queries; trace linkage opens relevant trace and highlights io_mode; documented runbook and test cases.

Design notes and trade-offs:
- Sampling vs completeness: full retention of high-cardinality labels (model_version + route + io_mode) is expensive; we will use two-tier retention: high-cardinality (model_version) kept at 7d raw + aggregated rollups at 90d; this reduces cost but still supports rollouts.
- Metric aggregation: compute percentile histograms in ClickHouse with the approximated t-digest approach used by current metrics pipeline. Expect +/- 1–3% error at p99; note in dashboard footnote.
- Traces: we will add a small mandatory io_mode tag on request entry to avoid expensive heuristics. Backend runtimes must populate io_mode before middleware.

Implementation plan (high level):
1) Instrumentation PR (tracing + metrics tags) — owner: Marco — target merge 2025-01-17.
2) Pipeline changes: ClickHouse schema updates, rollup job config — owner: Infra (Ravi) — target 2025-01-20.
3) Dashboard build: frontend panels + queries + UX toggles — owner: Celia Huang — target 2025-01-27.
4) Test & validate with synthetic replay workload (streaming bursts + blocking baseline) — owner: SRE — target 2025-01-30.
5) Ship and enable SLI-based alerts for a pilot set of routes (payments-api, chat-gen, embedding-batch) — target 2025-02-05.

Links to artifacts: see attachments.

Notes for reviewers:
- Pay attention to the cardinality mitigation plan (two-tier retention).
- Verify the io_mode contract in runtimes: "streaming" must be set for any HTTP streaming/gRPC bidi flows; otherwise set "blocking".
- Ensure SLI thresholds are parameterized per-customer tier (hosted vs dedicated).
